slot.subtopic: Cross product and angle between vectors
slot.brief: Given vectors with dot product equal to cross-product magnitude, determine the angle between them.

stem: If $\vec u=(\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k)\times(2\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)$ and $\vec v=-3\hat i+12\hat j+3\hat k$, find the angle between them.

verdicts.working: \(\vec u=(-6,6,-3)\). Then \(\vec u\cdot\vec v=81\), \(|\vec u|=9\), and \(|\vec v|=9\sqrt2\), so \(\cos\theta=1/\sqrt2\) and \(\theta=45^\circ\).

working:
$\vec u=-6\hat i+6\hat j-3\hat k$; $\vec u\cdot\vec v=81$. $\vec u\times\vec v=54\hat i+27\hat j-54\hat k$, so $|\vec u\times\vec v|=81$. Also $|\vec u||\vec v|=81\sqrt2$. Thus $\cos\theta=\sin\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\theta=45^\circ$.

Independent check: \(\vec u=(-6,6,-3)\). Then \(\vec u\cdot\vec v=81\), \(|\vec u|=9\), and \(|\vec v|=9\sqrt2\), so \(\cos\theta=1/\sqrt2\) and \(\theta=45^\circ\).
solution:
Using the cross-product formula, $\vec u=-6\hat i+6\hat j-3\hat k$. Hence $\vec u\cdot\vec v=81$, $|\vec u|=9$ and $|\vec v|=9\sqrt2$.
$$\cos\theta=\frac{\vec u\cdot\vec v}{|\vec u||\vec v|}=\frac{81}{81\sqrt2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$$
Therefore, $\theta=45^\circ$.
